items.title: In Retrograde release new demo ‘Cold Read’
items.summary: Sacramento band In Retrograde released the five-track demo "Cold Read" on Bandcamp on October 12, 2026, a name-your-price digital album.
items.fullText:
Sacramento, California band In Retrograde released the five-track demo “Cold Read” on Bandcamp on October 12, 2026. The release pairs two newly mixed older songs with two newer tracks and closes on the title cut.

The tracklist runs: “Shattered Sun (2026 mix)” (3:38), “Man Love” (2:46), “Italian Disco (2026 mix)” (3:29), “Italian Disco II” (3:52) and “Cold Read” (4:10).

“Cold Read” is available as a name-your-price digital album on Bandcamp, with a $5 minimum.

About In Retrograde

In Retrograde is a goth and post-punk band from Sacramento, California. The band’s earliest release on its own Bandcamp page is the album “Aries,” from January 2019. “Californian Misery” came out in October 2020. The single “Italian Disco” followed in September 2022, and the album “Strait of Messina” arrived the next month. “The Lovers” came out in April 2023, then “Samsara/Dharma” in March 2024.

items.title: Machine Command release ‘Uncontrolable’ ahead of 2027 album
items.summary: Rotterdam EBM duo Machine Command released "Uncontrolable" on 2 November 2026, a two-track single previewing an untitled album due spring 2027.
items.fullText:
Rotterdam EBM duo Machine Command released “Uncontrolable” on 2 November 2026, a two-track digital single that precedes an as yet untitled album scheduled for spring 2027.

Annemarie Janssen wrote the lyrics and Pieter Winkelaar the music. The duo describes the title track as a piece about machine intelligence turning on its makers: “It’s about conceited self-assured and self learning beings who threaten to wipe out humanity.”

The B-side is a remix of the album track “Predators” by The Peoples Republic Of Europe. The source track runs at 165 BPM, and the remixer moved it out of EBM tempo entirely. Machine Command stated that The Peoples Republic Of Europe “transformed the fast paced EBM to Drum& bass!”

“Uncontrolable” runs 4:30 and the “Predators” remix 3:50. Both tracks are available as a digital single on Bandcamp. The cover photo is credited to Ionut and the artwork design to Design Tiger Design.

About Machine Command

Machine Command formed in 2013 in Rotterdam, The Netherlands, as a duo playing EBM. The project lists KRAT on electronics and JAANSEN on vocals.

The duo has built a long run of self-released digital titles through Bandcamp, among them “Tetrarchy E.P.”, “To The Point”, “Without Fear EP”, “New Socialism”, “Not Doing It”, “Stampfbereit”, “Without Fear V2.0”, “Two Point Zero”, “Die Rote Linie”, “Decline and Rise Again”, “Nuke It from Orbit”, “Cathected” and “Rage”. Side-Line covered the band in November 2024 when they issued the Machine Command present EBM infested ‘Affected’ album, the release that preceded the current run of singles.

The remixer on the new B-side has his own history in Side-Line’s pages. The Peoples Republic Of Europe appeared on the site in August 2013 with the New ‘Feel The Power’ album by The Peoples Republic Of Europe out now item.

“Uncontrolable” is the second single the duo has drawn from those album sessions.

items.title: Liars share ‘Beat Creep Some Eyes’ video
items.summary: Liars released a video for "Beat Creep Some Eyes", from their album "A Ban On Plastic Bag Bans", out 5 March 2027 on Mute, and set a London date.
items.fullText:
Liars released a video for “Beat Creep Some Eyes”, the latest track from their forthcoming eleventh studio album, “A Ban On Plastic Bag Bans”, due 5 March 2027 on Mute.

The video was shot by visual collaborator Clemens Habicht on an obsolete 3D camera in and around Kalamazoo, Michigan, the city that inspired the album, after Angus Andrew relocated there with his family. Discussing the track, Andrew said: “Sometimes I think the strangest thing isn’t that the world is absurd, but how quickly we get used to it. You can find yourself living inside something completely ridiculous and, after a while, it just becomes Tuesday.”

Liars announced “A Ban On Plastic Bag Bans” in September; “Beat Creep Some Eyes” follows lead track “Ice Pick, Kalamazoo” as the second piece of music shared from the record. The album was written and recorded between the United States and Australia, where Andrew now lives, with Laurence Pike and Cameron Deyell, both collaborators on 2021’s “The Apple Drop”.

Liars also confirmed a London show at Village Underground on 15 May 2027, with tickets on sale from 10am on 6 November. The band play Drum’s Not Dead 20th-anniversary shows at Phoenix Central Park in Sydney on 26 and 27 November 2026.

“A Ban On Plastic Bag Bans” tracklist: “Happy Or Not”, “Ice Pick, Kalamazoo”, “Laced Plume”, “Urgent As Always”, “Deep Deeper”, “Disaster Tropes”, “Beat Creep Some Eyes”, “Real Time Trespasser”, “SHAME!”, “Retention Arc”, “Out Of Order”.

The album will be released on vinyl, CD and digitally through Mute.

About Liars

Liars formed in New York in 2000 around Angus Andrew. The band’s catalogue spans “They Threw Us All In A Trench And Stuck A Monument On Top” (2001), “Drums Not Dead” (2006), “TFCF” (2017) and “The Apple Drop” (2021). After “The Apple Drop”, Andrew paused making music to found the record label No Gold, before relocating to Kalamazoo, Michigan, an experience that shaped “A Ban On Plastic Bag Bans”. The album reunites Andrew with “The Apple Drop” collaborators Laurence Pike and Cameron Deyell, and is set for release on 5 March 2027 through Mute, preceded by the singles “Ice Pick, Kalamazoo” and “Beat Creep Some Eyes”.

items.title: Accessory open pre-orders for ‘Outrun The End’ vinyl
items.summary: German electro act Accessory opened pre-orders for "Outrun The End", a nine-track vinyl collection out 27 November via Infacted Recordings.
items.fullText:
German electro act Accessory opened pre-orders on 4 November for “Outrun The End”, a nine-track vinyl collection due 27 November 2026 through Infacted Recordings, pressed in a limited edition of 200 copies worldwide.

“Outrun The End” draws nine tracks from Accessory’s catalogue, including “Dark Gothic Queen,” “Outrun the Gun,” “Deadline” and “No Man Covers.” The B-side opens with Feindflug’s remix of “War of Emotions.”

Tracklist:

Side A: “Dark Gothic Queen,” “Outrun the Gun,” “Deadline,” “Shout It Out,” “No Man Covers”

Side B: “War of Emotions” (Feindflug remix), “What The Hell,” “Bad Conditions,” “Lifesaver”

“Outrun The End” is available as a black 12″ vinyl pressing through Infacted Recordings.

About Accessory

Accessory’s history goes back to 1994, when Dirk Steyer and Kay Resch started the project in Chemnitz, Germany, under the name Voices of Darkness. Two years later, they renamed the project Accessory. Over the following decades, the duo released albums including “Jukka2147.de” (2001), “Titan” (2003), “More Than Machinery” (2008) and “Elektrik” (2019), sharing stages with acts such as And One and Hocico. “Outrun The End” brings together nine tracks spanning that catalogue on a limited vinyl pressing through Infacted Recordings.

items.title: Seances share video for Assemblage 23’s remix of debut single ‘Fade’
items.summary: Milwaukee post-punk band Seances release a video for "Fade (Assemblage 23 Rmx)", Tom Shear's remix of their debut single, directed by Kyle Arpke.
items.fullText:
Milwaukee post-punk band Seances have released a video for “Fade (Assemblage 23 Rmx)”, Tom Shear’s remix of their debut single “Fade”, retitled “Killing Karma” for the clip. The remix came out on Bandcamp on 31 October 2026; the video, directed and edited by Kyle Lloyd Arpke with artwork by Ashley Altadonna of Tall Lady Productions, follows now.

Seances is the project of Eric Arsnow (vocals, bass, guitar, drums, programming) and guitarist Jason Kartz, who helped develop “Fade” from Arsnow’s initial sketches; Dexter and Paxton Arsnow contribute backing vocals. Arsnow formed Seances after seeing The Chameleons play in Milwaukee in 2023, and cites The Cure and Joy Division as influences alongside the Metropolis, Wax Trax! and Cleopatra label compilations. Shear’s remix, as Assemblage 23, adds an electronic layer to the band’s post-punk arrangement of “Fade”.

Arsnow described working with Shear on the remix: “Being able to work with Assemblage 23 on this remix of Fade was a dream come true.”

“Fade” first appeared on Seances’ debut album “Power Is A Phantom”. The band’s live line-up draws on members with ties to The Promise Ring, Masked Intruder, Tigernite, Fight Dice and BvsMV, and a second album, “Silent Salvation”, is planned for 2027. On 23 October 2026 the band released “Tame”, a name-your-price Bandcamp track dedicated to Arsnow’s late friend Francisco Ramirez, with proceeds passed to a fundraiser for Ramirez’s daughter.

About Seances

Seances are a post-punk band from Milwaukee, Wisconsin, formed by Eric Arsnow after seeing The Chameleons perform in the city in 2023. Arsnow writes and records as the project’s core member, playing vocals, bass, guitar, drums and programming, with guitarist Jason Kartz contributing to arrangements including “Fade”, and Dexter and Paxton Arsnow on backing vocals. The band’s sound draws on The Cure and Joy Division, filtered through the Metropolis, Wax Trax! and Cleopatra label compilations Arsnow grew up listening to. Seances released their debut single “Weighted” in January 2025 ahead of their debut album “Power Is A Phantom”, which includes “Fade”. A second album, “Silent Salvation”, is due in 2027. The band’s live members have previously played with The Promise Ring, Masked Intruder, Tigernite, Fight Dice and BvsMV. The “Fade (Assemblage 23 Rmx)” video, released under the title “Killing Karma”, marks the band’s first collaboration with Tom Shear’s long-running electro-industrial project Assemblage 23.

items.title: Nightcrawler and Carmilla Sioux release ‘System Lies’ single and video
items.summary: Nightcrawler and Carmilla Sioux release "System Lies", the second single from Nightcrawler's forthcoming album "Uranium 235", with a video he directed.
items.fullText:
Spanish dark synth producer Nightcrawler and Barcelona-based DJ and producer Carmilla Sioux have released “System Lies”, a single combining industrial EBM with dark electro. It is the second single taken from Nightcrawler’s forthcoming album “Uranium 235”, out now on Bandcamp, backed by a music video Nightcrawler directed himself.

Nightcrawler produced, mixed and mastered “System Lies” at his own NC Sound Studio; the cover was designed by George Gold Design. The video places the two artists’ industrial EBM sound inside a dystopian setting of military formations, decaying apartment blocks and hospital corridors, with a control-room monitor reading “REACTOR 4, CRITICAL FAILURE” and graffiti spelling out the track’s title.

“System Lies” follows Nightcrawler’s digital album “Malevolent Forces” and his 2025 collaboration with Spammerheads, “Ghostless”. Carmilla Sioux, a former post-punk bassist now working across EBM, electro, new beat, Italo and acid house, founded the label and event platform From Hell To Disco in 2024 and also records as half of the duo Villanelle alongside Jessica Bellomo, focused on 1980s-rooted dark synth and new wave.

About Nightcrawler

Nightcrawler is the solo project of a Spanish producer who began making music in 2011, drawing on horror and science-fiction film scores for his sound. His album catalogue includes “Metropolis”, “Beware of the Humans” and “Visionary”, alongside the EPs “Perverse Frequencies” and “Dynamics of a Crash”. He has recorded with Antoni Maiovvi, Makeup & Vanity Set and S Y Z Y G Y X, and has played live at Primavera Sound and Eufònic. Side-Line previously covered his digital album “Malevolent Forces” and his 2025 single “Ghostless” with Spammerheads. “System Lies” is the second preview of his forthcoming album “Uranium 235”, pairing him with Carmilla Sioux, a Barcelona producer and DJ who has played Urban Spree in Berlin, KHIDI in Tbilisi, Moog in Barcelona and the Grauzone festival.

items.title: “Hold Me Close in The Quiet Flame” —  Cork Post-Punk Duo Crá Croí Shares Visions From Irish Mythology and a Bleak Future in “Tá brón orm”
items.summary: Hold me close in the quiet flame Through shadowed paths I hear your name An ancient grove and a city emptied by catastrophe can provoke much the same unease: the… The post “Hold Me Close in The Quiet Flame” — Cork Post-Punk Duo Crá Croí Shares Visions From Iri
items.fullText:
Hold me close in the quiet flame
Through shadowed paths I hear your name

An ancient grove and a city emptied by catastrophe can provoke much the same unease: the sense that human lives have passed through a place without entirely leaving it. Voices carry across the water, footsteps return through the reeds, and the ground seems to retain the presence of its dead. The Irish mythological imagery of Cork duo Crá Croí‘s debut album, Tá brón orm—Irish for sadness is on me—finds a troubled tenderness in these encounters. Its groves and bogs hold the possibility of reunion alongside the danger of following something beyond the familiar world.

Set those images beside the apocalyptic imagination of the 1980s, and the distance between an ancient burial place and a ruined street begins to narrow. Both confront the living with traces of people they can no longer reach. Nuclear destruction brings that estrangement into ordinary rooms: a kettle, a pair of curtains, instructions promising protection when protection has become impossible. The dread lies in the persistence of familiar things after their meaning has changed. A forest that calls someone home and a house that can no longer shelter its occupants ask related questions about belonging, mortality, and the promises people need to believe.

Across these eleven songs of Tá brón orm, the desire to feel something real, hold another person, or find a way home survives amid the images of ash and ancient ground. Beauty carries an element of danger, while affection offers a reason to keep moving toward an uncertain future. Crá Croí gives that tension melodic form, setting repeating synth figures and resonant guitars around a voice capable of both intimate address and expansive release.

Released independently on October 30, 2026, the album was produced entirely by the duo. RG takes charge of the music, lyrics, instruments, drum machines, production, mixing, and mastering, while CD lends vocals, co-production, and the album’s hand-painted cover. Their post-punk, new wave, and darkwave arrangements turn on memorable melodic motifs, with guitars and synthesizers often merging into a single, elusive texture. Against that cool electronic precision, CD’s voice shifts from deep crooning to fervent singing and measured spoken passages.

Post-Punk.com previously followed the band’s five standalone singles: Radiation Romance, Fires At Dawn, Feeding The Fear, Lost In The Electric Blood, and Flesh Machines. Those songs preceded the album’s new material, introduced by the singles Lord Of The Wild, Black Snow, and Just Another Day. Across the full-length, the duo’s growing confidence comes through in the patient development of their arrangements and the ease with which their hooks move between genres.

Snare splashes and Kraftwerk-like synth ripples open the album’s first track, On The Fringes, giving way to kick drums and an icy synthpop melody with a touch of giallo cinema. That recurring figure carries the arrangement as CD’s deep darkwave croon enters, with guitar textures adding detail around the vocal hooks. The opener introduces Crá Croí’s expanding musical vocabulary, moving freely among new wave, post-punk, and darkwave through its catchy, melodic construction. Its lyrics search for authentic feeling amid coded routines and rigid rules, bringing a restless questioning to the song’s inviting surface.

Synth sighs spread over deep drumbeats as Kraftwerkian tones give Lord Of The Wild a synthwave cast. A melodic guitar figure enters before heavier guitar textures broaden the arrangement, accompanying CD’s rich, sonorous vocals. His delivery joins new wave melody to post-punk gravity, carrying the unabashed passion of the 1980s. That emotional generosity suits the lyrics’ ancient voices, sacred groves, and wandering king called home. The yearning reaches toward the natural world, seeking a connection with something older than the machinery surrounding it.

Metallic synth tones and sizzling percussion introduce Black Snow, with a short guitar melody supplying an anxious edge. A heavier guitar revs up before the drumbeat lands, setting fuller textures against more melodic figures. The vocals enter as the synth melody chimes through the arrangement. The song’s depth comes through in both the instrumental interplay and its thoughtful treatment of loss, with images of a devastated world accompanying a persistent search for light. The melody gives that search a direction through the surrounding ruin.

Rapidly repeated notes in a deeper synth register meet chiming tones at the beginning of Just Another Day. A few recurring guitar strums hold the introduction together until the beat kicks in, sending guitar melodies circling around the synthesizers. Those lines continually work off one another, giving the arrangement a distinctly new wave character. CD delivers another strong vocal performance, with apparent doubling lending his voice a chorus effect. The melodic exchanges accompany a biting account of counterfeit beauty, borrowed feeling, and daily routines that continue even as belief in them wears thin.

Over sighing synths, a rich, resonant guitar melody gives Sirens the feeling of a cool dawn. Once the drumbeat hits, the synthesizers surge into the melody introduced by the guitar, while heavier guitar textures support it from below. CD’s vocals rise euphorically through the arrangement, holding notes with an expansive, uplifting force. That exhilaration gives the lyrics’ irresistible call toward dangerous waters a persuasive musical counterpart: the melody makes the attraction easy to feel, even as the words lead toward the breakers.

Melodic, Kraftwerkian synth tones rise and fall through Threads, their slightly bassy colouring lending the opening a baroque character. The drumbeat and guitar textures enter beneath CD’s spoken-word delivery, which sets out the scene of devastation before turning to singing as the images of blurred faces appear. Around ninety seconds in, what sounds like a minimal guitar figure begins accenting his sung phrases, although guitar and synthesizer become increasingly difficult to distinguish. The arrangement cools around the two-minute mark: sighing synths surround the more prominent beat, accompanied by a deeper tone whose source remains ambiguous. Spoken vocals return, while the exceptionally catchy synth melody connects these changes through the song’s account of hunger, destruction, and isolation.

A strong drumbeat and deep bass guitar give Croí a Floodland-era Sisters of Mercy weight, with sizzling percussion beneath a higher, resonant guitar accent. Sighing synths introduce another Kraftwerkian melody with a baroque inflection, drawing guitars and electronics into an absorbing exchange. The production blends their tones so closely that individual sources can be difficult to distinguish. That repeating synth figure holds the arrangement together as low, sustained guitar stabs accent its emotional turns. CD’s chorus-treated vocals carry considerable pathos, particularly in his delivery of “Hold me close in the quiet flame”. The phrase sends a chill through the song, holding darkness and uplift together through the sheer passion of his singing.

Whispers In The Sea takes its time reaching the vocal, opening with rich, sustained guitars reverberating over lightly sizzling percussion. A kick drum establishes a heartbeat beneath the synthwave melody and sighing pads, while what sounds like bass guitar hums underneath. Hi-hat splashes suggest waves meeting the shore throughout the extended introduction. The instrumental lines feel more distinct here, with delayed guitar notes resonating against the synthesizers, their exchanges giving the music an oceanic breadth. CD’s rich, sonorous singing suggests a solitary figure looking out to sea and beyond it toward the horizon. The lyrics’ wish to be carried home, to recover a bond with what has been lost, suits this peaceful and uplifting contemplation.

Reverb gives the baroque, Kraftwerkian synth melody of Swords Into Ploughshares an expansive reach. Sighing pads, sizzling percussion, deep bass, and weighty drums gather around the figure, with a firm rhythmic emphasis keeping the arrangement moving. The melody maintains a measured pace, allowing its appeal to develop through repetition. CD enters with something of a prog-rock serenade, his singing settling naturally into the dreamy production. Just beyond two minutes, he switches to spoken words over the synth melody and beat before returning to the earlier sung delivery. His phrasing brings to mind the poetic singing of an Irish pub: a voice holding the room through the telling of a tale. That intimate quality gives the lyrics’ reflections on war, peace, and personal absence a conversational gravity.

Baroque, Kraftwerkian synths give Ghosts In The Bog a touch of giallo, their catchy repeating melody establishing the song’s central attraction. Sizzling drums and sighing pads surround sparse guitar tones, which recur within the synth figure until the melodies seem closely interlocked. Warm bass sits deep in the mix, supporting CD’s darkwave cadence as his delivery takes on a brighter new wave character. The synth melody holds its appeal throughout, accompanying lyrics of voices among the reeds and footsteps returning across ancient ground.

A thudding drumbeat and touches of hi-hat introduce When The Wind Blows, followed by the familiar synth tones and pads. The melody climbs and descends with the same easy appeal heard throughout the record. Lower in the mix, a bass guitar groove suggests a meeting between Peter Hook and Anka Wolbert, giving the electronics a supple foundation. CD croons the story before shifting into spoken delivery around forty-five seconds in; a gentle guitar melody sits beneath his words, leading into the return of his main sung vocal. The lyrics follow people trusting instructions and familiar domestic habits as catastrophe overtakes them, with affection persisting through their bewilderment. It is a strong closing track, bringing the album’s melodic assurance and poetic delivery together.

Crá Croí is a band that keeps getting better, and Tá brón orm gives that progress room to be heard across a full album. RG’s interlocking melodies reward attention to the arrangements, while CD gives the repeated figures an emotional scale that can turn an account of devastation into an intimate address. The recurring synth vocabulary establishes a recognisable identity; the changes in guitar weight, vocal delivery, and instrumental clarity keep the songs distinct. This is a confident full-length debut, with enough feeling in its melodies to carry forward its bleakest subjects.

Tá brón orm is out now. Listen to the album below and order it here.

items.title: Covenant’s ‘The Blinding Dark’ turns 10 on 4 November
items.summary: Dependent Records released Covenant's "The Blinding Dark" on 4 November 2016. The Swedish EBM act's ninth studio album turns 10 this year.
items.fullText:
Covenant released their ninth studio album, “The Blinding Dark”, through Dependent Records on 4 November 2016, with Metropolis Records handling the North American release. The Swedish electronic body music duo’s record turns 10 this year.

Joakim Montelius described the record around release as the band’s bleakest work to date, but not a resigned one: “It’s a very dark one, probably the darkest music we have ever made. […] But it’s not a beaten, sullen darkness. It’s a defiant one.” He called the album “much more introspective” than its predecessor, the “Sound Mirrors” EP, and described the shift as consistent with the band’s approach: “Covenant’s basic principle is to always evolve: change is the only constant.”

“The Blinding Dark” runs eleven tracks: “Fulwell”, “I Close My Eyes”, “Morning Star”, “Cold Reading”, “A Rider on a White Horse”, “Interlude”, “Dies Irae”, “Sound Mirrors (Fulwell)”, “Interlude”, “If I Give My Soul” and “Summon Your Spirit”. Eskil Simonsson handled songwriting and vocals, with Montelius on programming. Daniel Myer and Daniel Jonasson joined the touring line-up on live keyboards. Dependent issued the album on CD, a deluxe 2CD edition adding a bonus disc titled “Psychonaut”, and a limited vinyl pressing, alongside the digital release.

Side-Line tracked the release through 2016: the “Sound Mirrors” EP in August, the boxset pre-order in September, and a release-week interview in which Montelius discussed the album’s tone directly. The accompanying European tour, with support from Faderhead and Iszoloscope, opened in Odense on 29 October 2016 and continued into the following spring. “The Blinding Dark” follows two other Covenant anniversary pieces on Side-Line this year, for “Leaving Babylon” and “Northern Light”.

About Covenant

Eskil Simonsson, Joakim Montelius and Clas Nachmanson formed Covenant in 1986, three friends from Helsingborg, Sweden who were then studying in Lund. They settled on the band’s name in 1988. After attending one of Front 242’s first Scandinavian shows, the trio built a studio in Nachmanson’s bedroom and began recording. “The Replicant” appeared on a Memento Materia compilation in 1992, leading to the debut album “Dreams of a Cryotank” in 1994 and the “Figurehead” EP the following year.

“Sequencer” followed in 1996, backed by a tour with Haujobb and Steril, then the “Theremin” EP in 1997 and “Europa” in 1998. The band moved labels in 1999, joining Dependent in Europe and Metropolis Records in the United States after Metropolis took over their prior US distributor’s catalogue. “United States of Mind” and the live album “Synergy” both followed in 2000, and Sony’s Ka2 division handled the European release of “Northern Light” in 2002.

“Skyshaper” arrived in 2006. Nachmanson left the band the following year and was replaced by Daniel Myer of Haujobb. The road-movie DVD “In Transit” came out in October 2007. “Modern Ruin”, released in 2011, was the first studio album with Myer as a core member. “Leaving Babylon” followed in September 2013, after the “Last Dance” EP that June.

“The Blinding Dark” arrived in November 2016, trailed by the “Sound Mirrors” single and carried on tour across Germany, Italy, Spain, Portugal, France, Greece and Finland into 2017. The “Fieldworks: Exkursion” EP followed in 2019, the year Covenant headlined the Terminus Festival in Calgary. Touring member Andreas Catjar-Danielsson died in July 2024. Covenant released the charity EP “Andreas” on Dependent Records in his memory in October 2025. Ten years after “The Blinding Dark”, Simonsson and Montelius remain the band’s core songwriting unit.

items.title: ProtoU – The Infinite Recall (Digital/CD Album – Cryo Chamber)
items.summary: With the album “The Infinite Recall,” Ukrainian artist Sasha Puzan has released her first record...
items.fullText:
With the album “The Infinite Recall,” Ukrainian artist Sasha Puzan has released her first record of the year. Over the past few years, she has been remarkably prolific, releasing an impressive number of productions, including numerous collaborations. This time, she draws inspiration from pure science fiction: a world governed by an intelligent system designed to ensure continuous improvement and prevent any form of escalation, yet one in which cracks and flaws inevitably begin to emerge.

Those familiar with this artist’s refined Cinematic style may be somewhat surprised by this album. While she remains true to what I would describe as Cinematic music, the soundscape has shifted into an entirely different dimension. The tracks possess a deep, abyssal quality and unfold gradually. They never quite reach a conventional climax; instead, they evolve organically, creating a genuine sense of movement. The album also incorporates spoken-word elements that clearly allude to AI, leaving us wondering whether the artist is encouraging us to place greater trust in artificial intelligence or, conversely, suggesting that it can never be fully trusted. Musically, she has succeeded in crafting a remarkable record that departs from the darker character of some of her earlier work, exploring a different, more mysterious atmosphere. It is a compelling achievement, not least because every track is meticulously crafted, with subtle sounds and effects adding depth and detail to the overall soundscape.

If AI as main theme can inspire artists to create music like this, then there is still hope for the future. (Rating:8).

Listen to “Achromic (A Colorless Void Where The Truth Hides”:

About ProtoU

ProtoU is a dark-ambient and cinematic project by Ukrainian artist Sasha Puzan, credited in earlier Side-Line coverage as Sasha Cats. She released the joint album “Earth Songs” with Dronny Darko in 2015, followed by her solo debut “Lost Here” in 2016 on Cryo Chamber, then the second album “Khmaoch” the same year. A collaboration with Alphaxone, “Stardust”, followed in 2017. Her most recent solo album, “Dark Orbit”, came out in 2025. ProtoU now returns with “The Infinite Recall”.

items.title: Nightcrawler and Carmilla Sioux Expose the Machinery of Deception in “System Lies”
items.summary: “Everything is under control” becomes a particularly unconvincing reassurance when the officials delivering it are wearing gas masks. Screens repeat the message, documents disappear into a shredder, and a reactor… The post Nightcrawler and Carmilla Sioux Expos
items.fullText:
“Everything is under control” becomes a particularly unconvincing reassurance when the officials delivering it are wearing gas masks. Screens repeat the message, documents disappear into a shredder, and a reactor heads toward catastrophe. In Nightcrawler and Carmilla Sioux’s video for System Lies, public relations remains a functioning department well into the apocalypse. The authorities have plenty to say, provided nobody expects any of it to be true.

The Spanish electronic producer joins forces with the Barcelona-based DJ and producer for the second single from his forthcoming album, Uranium 235. Combining industrial EBM with dark electro, System Lies examines how institutions manipulate information and conceal the truth from the citizens whose lives depend upon it.

Deep, ominous bass synths open a channel for thick industrial drums, piston pulses, with cold electronic textures hanging above the rhythm. Humming, buzzing, and murmured voices crowd the mix, suggesting messages picked up through a wall or a damaged receiver. When the beat breaks, electronic shudders take over, and a ringing tone begins to resemble an exhausted alarm. Its blurred edges leave open the possibility of a voice buried inside the machinery.

Muffled male communiques drift across the track, their words too obscured to make out. That effect suits the subject: communication continues while meaning remains frustratingly inaccessible. As the drums return, the wailing tone persists above them. Later, mechanical noises and repeating EBM-techno sequences tighten the arrangement, spiraling toward the finish with the sensation of a machine accelerating beyond its operators’ control.

Created by Nightcrawler, the clip gives those uneasy transmissions an Orwellian setting of military formations, decaying apartment blocks, and official insignia stamped across public life. Protesters ask for the truth while the state broadcasts reassurance; a control-room monitor supplies the more useful bulletin: “REACTOR 4 — CRITICAL FAILURE.” Hospital corridors, rows of body bags, and the ruined power station expose the cost of that deception. Its sickly yellow-green palette makes the whole place seem contaminated before the warning symbols appear, while burning state vehicles and “SYSTEM LIES” graffiti give the population’s anger a blunt vocabulary.

Watch the video for System Lies below:

Nightcrawler began making music in 2011, drawing on horror and science-fiction scores. Albums including Metropolis, Beware of the Humans, and Visionary established that cinematic foundation, while the later EPs Perverse Frequencies and Dynamics of a Crash pursued further electronic experiments. His collaborators have included Antoni Maiovvi, Makeup & Vanity Set, and S Y Z Y G Y X, with live appearances at festivals including Primavera Sound and Eufònic.

Carmilla Sioux brings a background in post-punk bass playing to her work across EBM, electro, new beat, Italo, acid, and techno. Her DJ appearances include Urban Spree in Berlin, KHIDI in Tbilisi, and Barcelona’s Moog, alongside Grauzone festival. In 2024, she founded From Hell To Disco, a label and event platform encompassing releases, podcasts, and curated events. She also partners with Jessica Bellomo in Villanelle, exploring dark synth, new wave, and electronic music rooted in the 1980s.

System Lies was produced, mixed, and mastered by Nightcrawler at NC Sound Studio, with cover design by George Gold Design. The single is out now through Nightcrawler Music.

items.title: Takeshi Nishimoto and Hiroshi Watanabe announce ‘Curving Time’
items.summary: Takeshi Nishimoto and Hiroshi Watanabe release the album "Curving Time" on Lo Recordings on 6 November 2026, recorded over twelve years.
items.fullText:
Takeshi Nishimoto and Hiroshi Watanabe release their first collaborative album, “Curving Time,” on 6 November 2026 through Lo Recordings.

Nishimoto plays acoustic and classical guitars, electric guitar, loops and fretless bass. Watanabe handles keyboards, synth bass, electronics and programming, and recorded and mixed the album. The eight tracks were recorded on and off over twelve years, with sessions split between Watanabe’s private studio in Japan and Nishimoto’s living-room studio in Berlin, Germany.

The album’s eight tracks are:

  1. “Winding Air”
  2. “Pivotal Point”
  3. “Layer of Images”
  4. “Serendipity”
  5. “Where To”
  6. “Puzzling”
  7. “Empty Park”
  8. “After The Time”

Nishimoto plays fretless bass on “Pivotal Point” in addition to the guitar parts that run through the record. Lo Recordings issued “Empty Park,” track seven, as the album’s first single on 18 September 2026.

“Curving Time” is available on limited cassette and digitally, with pre-orders open through Lo Recordings and advance streaming through the label’s SoundCloud page.

About Takeshi Nishimoto and Hiroshi Watanabe

Takeshi Nishimoto is a Japanese guitarist, composer, multi-instrumentalist and educator who composes and performs across contemporary classical, ambient, electronic and cross-cultural music. He trained classically at the University of Southern California and developed a style rooted in European classical repertoire, North Indian classical music, jazz and minimalist composition. He has collaborated with John Tejada, Burnt Friedman, Robert Lippok and Mike Shannon, and released music through City Centre Offices, Sonic Pieces, Nonplace, Tho, New Kanada, Cynosure Recordings and Palette Recordings.

Hiroshi Watanabe is a Tokyo-born electronic music producer and DJ who produces melodic techno and ambient tracks. He studied synthesizers at Berklee College of Music, spent time in New York’s underground scene, then returned to Japan. He also records under the alias Kaito, with releases through Kompakt and Derrick May’s Transmat Records, and more recently through InFiné.

“Curving Time” is the first album Nishimoto and Watanabe have made together, drawing on more than twenty years each in acoustic and electronic music. It arrives on Lo Recordings on 6 November 2026.

items.title: Oui Plastique announce second album ‘Forever Will Be Over Before You Know It’
items.summary: Oui Plastique release new album "Forever Will Be Over Before You Know It" via Town and Towers Records on 27 November 2026.
items.fullText:
Danish/UK electronic duo Oui Plastique will release their second studio album, “Forever Will Be Over Before You Know It”, through Scandinavian label Town and Towers Records on 27 November 2026. The 14-track record follows the duo’s 2022 debut, “Fraternity Of Strangers”, and arrives four years after that release.

Oui Plastique is the project of Martin Nyrup and James Thomas. The duo describe the new album as retaining the melodic sensibility and electronic foundations of their debut while expanding into a broader sonic palette and richer arrangements. “Forever Will Be Over Before You Know It” will be available on all major digital platforms, as well as on CD and vinyl.

Tracklist

  1. We Were Always Dying
  2. Messiah
  3. Black Skies
  4. Revival
  5. September (feat. Vika Jaffe)
  6. Ultraviolet
  7. Linger
  8. Nothing Lasts Forever
  9. Summer Sun’s Adore
  10. Spirit
  11. For The Cry Of Anguish
  12. Release Me
  13. Discontented (feat. Liat Zion)
  14. Oblivion
  15. The Persuaders Theme (bonus track)
  16. Spejlfald (bonus track)

Three of the album’s tracks, “Linger”, “Spirit” and “For The Cry Of Anguish”, were previously issued as standalone singles through Town and Towers Records over the course of 2026, with Side-Line covering each release. “For The Cry Of Anguish”, issued on 2 October 2026, was announced at the time as the fourth and final single before the album.

About Oui Plastique

Oui Plastique is an electronic duo from Denmark formed by Martin Nyrup and James Thomas. The project’s debut album, “Fraternity Of Strangers”, was released in 2022 through ScentAir Records.

In August 2025, the duo released the “UnMute” EP through Town and Towers Records, featuring a cover of a Martin Gore (Depeche Mode) track. Throughout 2026, Oui Plastique issued a run of singles through the same label ahead of their second album: “Linger” on 16 June, “Spirit” on 12 August, and “For The Cry Of Anguish” on 2 October, the last of these billed as the final single before the album proper.

“Forever Will Be Over Before You Know It”, the duo’s second studio album, follows through Town and Towers Records on 27 November 2026. The label’s roster also includes fellow Scandinavian act CRED, whose single “Father” was released through Town and Towers Records earlier in November 2026.

items.title: State Of The Union releases ‘Until Death Do Us Apart’
items.summary: State Of The Union released the single "Until Death Do Us Apart" on 1 November 2026, a Dia de los Muertos-themed track on Bandcamp.
items.fullText:
Los Angeles electronic industrial project State Of The Union has released the single “Until Death Do Us Apart,” out 1 November 2026 as a self-released digital track on Bandcamp.

Johann Sebastian, the artist behind State Of The Union, said the song “honors the beautiful Mexican tradition of Dia de los Muertos, a time to remember and celebrate the lives of those we love who are no longer with us.” The version now live on Bandcamp is the final mastered edition, replacing a pre-master uploaded on 30 October 2026.

“Until Death Do Us Apart” follows State Of The Union’s single “When Daylight Dies,” released on Bandcamp on 5 October 2026, the project’s first new material since the 2023 singles “Purgatory” and “Lifeline.”

About State Of The Union

State Of The Union is a Los Angeles electronic industrial and futurepop project fronted by Johann Sebastian, with drummer Jimmy Nimra contributing to past studio releases. The project’s prior full-length, “Impendum,” came out in 2004. State Of The Union signed to Infacted Recordings and released the digital EP “Mindless” in November 2018, followed by the CD album “Indupop” and the digital EP “Industrial Slither / Remixes” in early 2019, and the EP “Bad Flower” in 2020, all on Infacted Recordings.

The project went quiet for three years before returning with the singles “Purgatory” in August 2023 and “Lifeline” in October 2023. It resurfaced again in October 2026 with “When Daylight Dies,” followed a month later by “Until Death Do Us Apart,” its Dia de los Muertos-themed single released on 1 November 2026.

items.title: Ahrayeph marks 30th anniversary with concert at J.C. De Klinker, Korinthians as special guest
items.summary: Gothic rock band Ahrayeph marks 30 years with a concert at J.C. De Klinker in Aarschot on 5 December 2026, with special guest Korinthians.
items.fullText:
Belgian progressive gothic rock band Ahrayeph marks 30 years as a project with a concert at J.C. De Klinker in Aarschot on Saturday 5 December 2026. Ghent post-punk quartet Korinthians joins as special guest, presenting songs from their new album “After Life”, released 23 October.

Ahrayeph is the project of Raf Ahrayeph, who founded the band in 1996. For the anniversary show he is joined by drummer Tom Veltens, formerly of Minus 273, and guitarist/multi-instrumentalist Yanes; the line-up is still completing its search for a bassist. The set is billed to span the band’s full three-decade catalogue, with the night closing out in a DJ set from Leuven-based D.J. Malcolm Nix.

Korinthians is a dance-postpunk quartet from Ghent that released “After Life” on 23 October as a digital album, vinyl LP and CD via Bandcamp. Side-Line interviewed the band in 2023 ahead of their album “A Major Walk”.

Ahrayeph’s 30th anniversary concert details

  • Saturday 5 December 2026 – J.C. De Klinker, Aarschot, Belgium, with special guest Korinthians and a closing DJ set by Malcolm Nix

About Ahrayeph

Ahrayeph began in the late spring of 1996 in Leuven, Belgium, when Raf Ahrayeph formed a band under the name Crucifire, drawing on The God Machine, Fields of the Nephilim, Paradise Lost, Type O Negative and other proto-goth acts of the 1980s. That line-up recorded a demo the following autumn and split up after about a year. Crucifire stayed dormant until 2000, when Raf revived the project as its sole member and renamed it Ahrayeph, moving away from the earlier metal influences toward a more organic, progressive sound closer to Pink Floyd, Marillion, Fields of the Nephilim, The God Machine, Killing Joke and Joy Division.

New songs followed, and by 2004 Ahrayeph had a new line-up, which played its first show in September 2007. The band’s debut album, “Marooned On Samsara”, came out in April 2008, but that line-up also proved short-lived. Raf spent the following years trying, without success, to hold a stable band together, and went fully solo in 2012.

For the next thirteen years, Ahrayeph operated as a one-man studio project, releasing the albums “AnimAElegy” and “Heavy Like The Ancient Sun” – the latter dedicated to his late friend James Blaast of Glasgow – along with regular singles and EPs. The fourth album, “The Final Hurt”, followed in 2025; Raf has described it as the band’s last full-length, with future releases to take the form of singles and EPs.

With that album out, Raf shifted his focus from the studio back to the stage, recruiting drummer Tom Veltens, formerly of Minus 273. The pair built up a live set through tryout shows in early 2026, backed by outlets including the Belgian gothic magazine Dark Entries. Guitarist and multi-instrumentalist Yanes joined over the summer, and the band is still looking for a bassist to round out the line-up. Ahrayeph marks its 30th anniversary on 5 December 2026 at J.C. De Klinker in Aarschot, with Korinthians as special guest and a closing set from D.J. Malcolm Nix.

items.title: Berlin Darknights Festival II reveals full line-up for Festsaal Kreuzberg
items.summary: Berlin Darknights Festival II runs 29-30 January 2027 at Festsaal Kreuzberg, with Funker Vogt, Covenant, Rotersand, [:SITD:] and S.P.O.C.K. confirmed.
items.fullText:
Berlin Darknights Festival returns for its second edition on 29 and 30 January 2027 at Festsaal Kreuzberg, expanding to two stages. Confirmed acts include Funker Vogt, [:SITD:], Blitz Union, Angels & Agony and Giant Crow on Friday, with Covenant, Rotersand, S.P.O.C.K., Morphose and CHROM headlining Saturday.

Following its inaugural edition, the festival returns to Festsaal Kreuzberg with an expanded programme distributed across two stages. It brings together musicians whose careers stretch back several decades alongside artists representing newer developments in electronic music.

Friday 29 January: Funker Vogt, [:SITD:], Blitz Union

Funker Vogt remains one of the most recognisable names in German electro-industrial music. Founded in 1995 by Gerrit Thomas and Jens Kästel, the project built its sound on forceful electronic sequences, aggressive vocal delivery and anthemic arrangements, with tracks such as “Tragic Hero” and “Gunman” becoming club favourites. [:SITD:], associated with vocalist Carsten Jacek, combines imposing rhythmic structures with atmospheric synthesizers across albums including “Stronghold”, “Dunkelziffer” and “Trauma: Ritual”.

Blitz Union, formed in Prague in 2019, bring a newer generation of industrial-influenced music, combining guitars, electronic dance rhythms and contemporary alternative-rock songwriting. Their second album “Evolution” was released in January 2026. The Dutch project Angels & Agony, founded by Reinier Kahle in 1995, adds a more melodic futurepop and synthpop dimension, while Hamburg’s Giant Crow draw on alternative country, post-punk and neo-psychedelia around singer and banjo player Nikolas Kuhl.

The second stage on Friday brings Hamburg trio Sono (Lennart A. Salomon, Florian Sikorski, Martin Weiland), Dresden’s Battle Scream, Swiss project Dunkelsucht led by Patrick Näf, Zoodrake (the work of Hilton Theissen, also known for AKANOID and Dark Millennium) and Devil-M.

Saturday 30 January: Covenant, Rotersand, S.P.O.C.K.

Covenant, the Swedish project fronted by Eskil Simonsson, headlines Saturday with a catalogue spanning “Sequencer”, “United States of Mind”, “Northern Light” and “Leaving Babylon”. Rotersand, established in 2002 by Rascal Nikov and Krischan Wesenberg, combines EBM, techno and trance with socially conscious songwriting, with 2025’s “Don’t Become the Thing You Hated” as a recent reference point.

S.P.O.C.K. bring their science-fiction-themed synthpop, built on tracks such as “Never Trust a Klingon” and “Silicon Dream”. Morphose, the project of Berlin-based composer Christoph Schauer, brings a cinematic dimension drawn from his work in film and television scoring, with past collaborators including Sono’s Lennart A. Salomon and Neuroticfish’s Sascha Klein. Gulvøss, created by Berlin musician Sven Wittmiß, contributes a more melancholic, introspective songwriting style across albums including “Sinners vs. Saints” and “The Perfect Symphony”.

The second stage on Saturday features CHROM, founded in 2007 by Christian Marquis and Thomas Winters and continued by Marquis alone since Winters’ departure in 2022. Also on the bill are The Second Sight, whose September 2026 album “Time for a Change” introduced flugelhorn into their arrangements, and KY. The evening also includes CS50, a programme marking the fiftieth birthday of Christian Schottstädt, known for his work with Forced To Mode.

About Berlin Darknights Festival

Berlin Darknights Festival launched with its first edition at Festsaal Kreuzberg, and returns for Berlin Darknights Festival II on 29-30 January 2027 with an expanded two-stage programme. The venue, on the banks of the Flutgraben canal in Kreuzberg, has hosted electronic and alternative acts for over two decades. The second edition brings together artists from German electro-industrial and EBM, alongside acts whose work extends into post-punk and cinematic electronic composition.

Berlin Darknights Festival II: dates, venue and tickets

  • Event: Berlin Darknights Festival II
  • Dates: 29-30 January 2027
  • Venue: Festsaal Kreuzberg, Am Flutgraben 2, 12435 Berlin, Germany
  • Doors: 3:00 PM daily, concerts begin 4:00 PM daily
  • Stages: Main Stage and Second Stage
  • Tickets: €75 per day or €125 for the weekend, plus advance booking fees, through the official festival shop

More information is available on the festival’s official website.

items.title: The Unnamed Fear release self-titled single ‘The Unnamed Fear’ with video
items.summary: Berlin industrial dark rock duo The Unnamed Fear released the single and video "The Unnamed Fear" on 31 October 2026, self-released.
items.fullText:
Berlin-based industrial dark rock duo The Unnamed Fear released the self-titled single “The Unnamed Fear,” together with a music video, on 31 October 2026. The track is self-released.

“The Unnamed Fear” is the duo’s second single, following their debut, “Hysteria.” The band describes the new track’s theme as the fear of something that has no face yet still exerts control. “For us the unnamed fear is the grief of abandonment and the ominous presence of something without a face. Call it trauma, call it the Big Other: we are all caught in this web,” the band said.

The Unnamed Fear consists of Alisha (vocals, visuals) and Anto (vocals, composition, guitars, lyrics). Their sound combines synthesizers, drum machines and industrial guitars. The band cites musical references ranging from L’Âme Immortelle to Assemblage 23 and Terminal Choice.

The video was filmed at Reel2Reel Studio in Berlin, based on a concept by Alisha. Set against a red backdrop, the duo perform as a faceless figure slowly emerges from the darkness. The figure gives the song its title but is never fully revealed.

About The Unnamed Fear

The Unnamed Fear is a Berlin-based industrial dark rock duo of Alisha, who handles vocals and the project’s visual concepts, and Anto, who contributes vocals, composition, guitars and lyrics. The band combines electronic beats, synthesizers and drum machines with industrial guitars, pairing two contrasting vocal styles across its material.

The duo released their debut single, “Hysteria,” on 9 October 2026, with an accompanying official video. “The Unnamed Fear” followed as their second single on 31 October 2026, again with a video, this one filmed at Reel2Reel Studio in Berlin around a concept by Alisha. Both releases are self-released.

items.title: CRED sets release date for new single ‘Father’
items.summary: Swedish synthpop duo CRED will release the single "Father" on 5 November 2026 through Town And Towers Records, with an official video the same day.
items.fullText:
Swedish synthpop duo CRED will release the single “Father” on 5 November 2026 through Town And Towers Records. An official video premieres on YouTube the same day at 21:00 CET.

“Father” explores the relationship between a son and his father, built around the repeated line “Father, guide me home.” The track pairs dark electronic textures with driving synth rhythms and melancholic melodies, drawing on the tradition of 1980s synthpop and post-punk.

CRED is the Swedish West Coast duo of Bjarne Sund and Hans Karlsson. The band was founded by Sund and Tony Berntsson in 2022, with Fredrik Bergman (also of Etage Neun) contributing as a guest vocalist in the early days. Karlsson later joined as a permanent vocalist, and Berntsson stepped away from the project in autumn 2025, leaving CRED to continue as a duo.

“Father” follows CRED’s single “Redemption,” released via Town And Towers in October 2025. The band’s two albums to date, “Songs From The Vault” (December 2025) and “Bleed” (April 2026), are both out on Town And Towers Records on CD and vinyl through Elastic Stage.

About CRED

CRED is a Swedish electronic duo from the country’s West Coast, founded by Bjarne Sund and Tony Berntsson in 2022. Drawing inspiration from 1980s synthpop acts such as Depeche Mode, OMD, Elegant Machinery and Pet Shop Boys, the pair built a sound centred on classic analog synthesizers, releasing early tracks including “Every Loss,” “Bleed” and “Chasing.”

Fredrik Bergman, also known from Etage Neun, contributed as a guest vocalist in the band’s early days. Hans Karlsson later joined as a permanent vocalist, a move that let CRED refine its sound further. In autumn 2025, Tony Berntsson stepped away from the project, and CRED continued as a duo of Sund and Karlsson.

In late summer 2025, CRED signed to the Danish label Town And Towers Records. The album “Songs From The Vault” followed in December 2025, and “Bleed” arrived in April 2026. The band’s next album, “Polaroid,” is in progress, with the label targeting a release in December 2026 or January 2027.

CRED’s single “Father” is set for release on 5 November 2026 via Town And Towers Records, with an official video premiering the same day.

items.title: New Model Army and Anja Huwe to headline Tomorrow’s Ghosts Festival 2027 in Whitby
items.summary: New Model Army and Anja Huwe headline Tomorrow's Ghosts Festival 2027 at Whitby Pavilion, 29 to 31 October, with Chameleons and David J.
items.fullText:
Tomorrow’s Ghosts Festival has confirmed its 2027 line-up, with New Model Army headlining the Saturday and Anja Huwe of Xmal Deutschland headlining the Friday. The Halloween Gathering takes place at Whitby Pavilion in Whitby, England, from 29 to 31 October 2027, organisers announced on 3 November 2026.

New Model Army’s Saturday set will be the band’s first Whitby appearance in more than four years and its third time topping the festival’s bill. Chameleons perform their 1983 album “Script of the Bridge” in full on the Friday, and David J of Bauhaus and Love and Rockets revisits the Love and Rockets album “Earth, Sun, Moon” alongside other tracks from his back catalogue.

Tomorrow’s Ghosts Festival 2027 lineup

Friday 29 October: Anja Huwe (Xmal Deutschland) headlines, with Chameleons performing “Script of the Bridge,” David J performing “Earth, Sun, Moon,” and Mouth Ulcers.

Saturday 30 October: New Model Army headlines, with Heartworms, Corpus Delicti and Mercy Girl.

Club night host Carpe Noctum returns on both nights. The weekend also includes a gothic and alternative market and additional events to be confirmed.

Tickets went on general sale on 2 November 2026 through the festival’s official site, with separate Friday, Saturday and weekend passes available. The event is open to ages 8 and up, with under-14s required to be accompanied by an adult; evening shows run from 6pm to a 2am curfew, and after-show club nights are restricted to those 18 and over.

As in previous years, the festival partners with the Sophie Lancaster Foundation, a charity opposing prejudice and hate crime. Vive Le Rock Magazine is the festival’s official media partner for 2027.

About Tomorrow’s Ghosts Festival

Tomorrow’s Ghosts Festival has run annually at Whitby Pavilion since 2018, held in the Yorkshire coastal town where Bram Stoker set much of “Dracula.” The Halloween Gathering combines club nights, a market and live music across a weekend built around goth, post-punk and darkwave acts, and has sold out every edition between 2022 and 2026.

Saturday’s headliner, New Model Army, formed in Bradford, West Yorkshire, in 1980 around vocalist and guitarist Justin Sullivan, bassist Stuart Morrow and drummer Phil Tompkins. Sullivan has remained the band’s only continuous member across sixteen studio albums, from 1984’s “Vengeance” to 2024’s “Unbroken.” The band’s current line-up also includes Dean White, Michael Dean and Ceri Monger.

Friday’s headliner, Anja Huwe, was the vocalist of Xmal Deutschland, a gothic rock band she formed with an all-female line-up in Hamburg in 1980. Xmal Deutschland released four studio albums between 1983 and 1989, including “Fetisch” and “Tocsin” on 4AD, before disbanding in 1990; the band’s early singles were reissued by Sacred Bones Records in 2024.

Manchester post-punk band Chameleons released “Script of the Bridge,” the album they perform in full at Whitby, in 1983. The band released the 2024 EP “Tomorrow Remember Yesterday” and the 2025 single “Saviours Are A Dangerous Thing” on Metropolis Records.

David J was a founding member of Bauhaus and later formed Love and Rockets with Daniel Ash and Kevin Haskins; he has also released a long run of solo material and discussed his demo-reworking album “Tracks From the Attic Revisited” with Side-Line in 2026. London act Heartworms, who play Saturday, announced its debut EP in 2023. French post-punk and gothic rock act Corpus Delicti, also on the Saturday bill, announced its album “Liminal” in October 2025.

Tomorrow’s Ghosts Festival returns to Whitby Pavilion from 29 to 31 October 2027, headlined by New Model Army and Anja Huwe.
